legal.summary: Defined as unlawful carnal knowledge of a woman or girl without consent (including consent obtained by force, threat, or false representation). This definition is gender-specific to female victims.
legal.penalty: Felony; sentencing varies by circumstance, up to death penalty in aggravated cases as defined by the courts.

legal.summary: A sexual act with a person under 18 years of age. Attempted defilement is a separate, lesser offence.
legal.penalty: Defilement: life imprisonment. Attempted defilement: up to 18 years.

legal.summary: Applies when the victim is under 14, the offender is HIV-positive, the offender is a parent, guardian or person in authority, the victim has a disability, or the offender is a repeat offender.
legal.penalty: Death sentence on conviction by the High Court; attempt carries life imprisonment.

legal.summary: A separate statute from the Penal Code covering physical, sexual, economic and emotional/psychological abuse between spouses or family members. It is gender-neutral and applies regardless of which partner is the survivor. Provides for protection orders.
legal.penalty: Varies; includes protection orders and criminal penalties for breach.

title.en: A note for male survivors of sexual assault

legal.summary: Because Section 123 (rape) applies only to female victims, a male survivor of sexual assault is generally not able to report it as 'rape' under that section. Male-on-female indecent assault falls under separate indecent-assault provisions. Same-sex sexual assault is often handled under Section 145 ('carnal knowledge against the order of nature'), which also broadly criminalises same-sex conduct — meaning a male survivor reporting a same-sex assault may risk that same statute being used against him. This is why Ekyama routes every report to a counsellor first, before any decision about police involvement is made, and never requires disclosure of an assailant's sex to access support.
